A hop's engine call runs on the mod thread
Serve the hop before the buffer: the hop overtakes the writes before it
Borrow without applying the buffer: the decision's own writes overtake the mod's buffered ones

name: Strict mode off in the guard: a read after the mod's write is answered from the old snapshot
The design note's rule: strict reads hop only after a write in the same event, so a later event reads a snapshot without the mod's earlier write

name: Borrow while the window applies the mod's own commands
Borrow ahead of a queued event: the decision overtakes the event before it
Wait for the mod: a decision with the mod busy waits until the mod is idle
A queued Frame is not replaced: Frames pile up behind a slow mod
Stop does not wake the hop waiter: the join waits on a hop nobody serves
No epoch check: a running call never traps after the stop
A failed mod is never joined
No deadline: the window stays open while the mod computes
Weak fairness on hops: every window's deadline can pass before its hop is served
A window closes on a waiting hop: the mod's wait counts as quiet
The overlap exit (run under the Quiet design's name) ignores a waiting hop: the window returns while the mod waits on it
